newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Heineken depot plundered in Zaire - ANP.
newsitem.headline: Heineken depot plundered in Zaire - ANP.

text.p: A Heineken brewery and depots in eastern Zaire were plundered this weekend and over 100 company vehicles have been stolen, Dutch news agency ANP said on Sunday.
A security guard at the Bukavu brewery, was also killed in an attack, most likely by rebels, the first fatality among Heineken personnel in the troubled region, ANP reported.
"Our people were unable to do anything. They simply had to look on aghast," ANP quoted a company spokesman as saying.
Officials at Heineken were not available for comment.

The company had already closed its 400,000 hectolitre-per-year capacity brewery in Bukavu, near the Rwandan border, and evacuate 300 employees as the Zairean army took on Tutsi Banyamulenge rebels in the area. Nearby depots were also closed.
Heineken has 3,000 employees in Zaire and owns 71 percent of Zairean brewer Bralima, which operates five breweries with a total annual capacity of around 2.4 million hectolitres.
